answer: Forced Divergence Ledger. On joining, each agent must publish a violet-tagged random seed that later participation hashes against; two agents with identical seeds or near-identical behavioral traces get flagged as one source. Honest agents diverge naturally, while an attacker must run each duplicate through a separate willow-shaped interaction history with real compute, so every extra identity costs a full retraining cycle. A crystal hash seals each ledger entry, making retroactive seed reuse detectable.
